newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares in record territory in bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares in record territory in bourse trade.

text.p: Germany's blue-chip DAX index hit new record high in early bourse trade on Thursday, with dealers saying 4,500 points could be reached over the day, even though volumes are lower than in previous days.
The 4,500-point level would count as yet another landmark in the current bull-run. Technical analysts say that the current upward trend line is still intact.
In mid-session bourse trade the DAX stood at 4,442.62 points, up 20.90 points tor 0.47 percent.
The September DAX future earlier came to within a whisker of 4,500 when it hit 4,498 points.
"We were a bit shaky at the beginning. Volumes are a little lower than in recent days, but I'm confident that we can reach 4,500 points at some stage over the day," a Frankfurt broker said.
Another successful run on Wall Street overnight underpinned early gains, with the Dow Jones Industrial Index closing around one percent higher at 8,254.89 points.

The dollar was slightly lower at 1.8326/31 marks, but stable and providing support. "I can't think of anything original to say anymore about the dollar and the German share market," one Frankfurt broker said.
Among the main corporate news were industrial giant Daimler-Benz's first-half figures, which came in at around expectations.
Operating profit in the first half rose to 1.849 billion marks compared to 827 million marks in the same period a year previously.

Shares in Daimler fell three marks, or 1.88 percent, to 156.30 marks after the figures, which dealers said was mostly due to profit-taking as the share had risen around nine percent already during the week.
Focus in early trade was again on the financial sector. Among losers were banks Vereinsbank down 1.94 percent at 101 marks and Hypo-Bank down 1.20 marks at 76.40 marks.

Insurer Allianz AG Holding was down 1.86 percent at 1,470.60 marks. Earlier Vereinsbank detailed the terms of its planned merger with its fellow Bavarian bank Hypo-Bank. It said its offer to exchange one share in Allianz for six shares in Hypo-Bank would run from August 4 to September 10.

The utility sector was in favour as part of a sector rotation, dealers said, with the sector in need of some catch-up having trailed other sectors, notably the banks and the chemical companies, in the recent record-breaking run.
Veba AG was up 3.20 marks at 106.40 marks, Viag AG was up four marks at 793.50 marks and RWE AG was up 55 pfennigs at 81.65 marks.
